passages.text:
### Reading Passage: Extract from *The Nightingale*

Long ago in China, the Emperor lived in the world's most beautiful palace, made of delicate **porcelain**. His garden was equally wondrous, filled with extraordinary flowers, some with tiny silver bells that tinkled gently. The garden was so vast it stretched into a great forest with tall trees and deep lakes, reaching down to the blue sea.

In this forest lived a nightingale. Its song was so lovely that even the poor fisherman, busy pulling in his nets at night, would pause to listen. 'Heavens, how beautiful!' he'd whisper before returning to his work. Travellers came from all over the world to see the Emperor's city. They admired the palace and garden, but upon hearing the nightingale, they all declared, 'That is the best thing of all!'. Books were written praising the city, but the nightingale was always described as the greatest treasure.

One day, the Emperor read one of these books. 'A nightingale?' he exclaimed. 'In my own kingdom, my own garden, and I've never heard of it? I must learn about my greatest treasure from a book?'. He summoned his gentleman-in-waiting. 'There's said to be a marvellous bird called a nightingale here,' said the Emperor. 'Why wasn't I told?'

'I've never heard it mentioned, Your Majesty,' the gentleman replied.

'It must come sing for me tonight!' the Emperor commanded.

### Literature Extract: Extract from *Dad...* by Zirsangkima

Bawihpuia had a particular trait unique from his friends, which was his **obsession** for writing and scribbling on anything, with anything. Even if a pen and paper was not available, he would write with anything available, writing about anything that came to mind, on anything—our walls, windows, mirrors were always filled with his handiwork. One time he was loitering around in the kitchen where his mother was stitching. He picked up a fallen needle and started to write, 'My name is ...' on the fridge when I spotted him. I called him inside our bedroom, and started reprimanding him—

'A needle is for stitching, not to write something on the fridge. The walls of the fridge are painted; if we write something with a needle it will leave a scratch and we will have to buy new paint to repaint it.'

He looked straight at me while I was speaking. I told him that every tool had its specific purpose, and that he should not repeat what he had done. After that I noticed that the writings on the walls and other surfaces slowly started to decrease.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct past continuous form of the verb: While the Emperor was resting, the nightingale ___ (sing) sweetly in the forest.
questions.hint: Use was/were + verb-ing for singular past continuous action.
questions.correctAnswer: was singing
questions.explanation: 'The nightingale' is a singular subject in the past continuous tense, requiring the auxiliary 'was' followed by 'singing'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct future continuous form of the verb: Tomorrow at this hour, the royal court ___ (listen) to the singer's melody.
questions.hint: The formula for future continuous is will/shall + be + verb-ing.
questions.correctAnswer: will be listening
questions.explanation: Future continuous indicates an ongoing action at a specific future moment, using 'will be' + '-ing' form ('listening').

questions.question: Choose the correct tense form to complete the sentence: The secretary ___ (type) a letter when the lights went out.
questions.hint: Identify the action that was ongoing in the past when another past event interrupted it.

options.text: was typing
options.explanation: Correct. Past continuous describes an action interrupted by another simple past event ('went out').

options.text: is typing
options.explanation: Incorrect. The clause 'when the lights went out' indicates the context is firmly in the past.

options.text: will be typing
options.explanation: Incorrect. Future tense cannot be combined with the past event 'went out'.

options.text: typed
options.explanation: Incorrect. An ongoing background interrupted action requires the continuous aspect.

questions.correctAnswer: was typing
questions.explanation: Past continuous tense ('was typing') expresses an ongoing past action interrupted by a shorter action in the simple past ('went out').

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the past continuous form: The curtains ___ (sway) in the gentle breeze all afternoon.
questions.hint: 'Curtains' is plural, so use were + verb-ing.
questions.correctAnswer: were swaying
questions.explanation: Since the subject 'curtains' is plural, the past continuous auxiliary verb 'were' is used with 'swaying'.

questions.question: Select the correct transformation of the sentence into the present continuous tense: 'Rishi drove to work yesterday.'
questions.hint: Use is/am/are + verb-ing and adjust temporal adverbs appropriately.

options.text: Rishi is driving to work today.
options.explanation: Correct. 'is driving' expresses the present continuous form accurately.

options.text: Rishi was driving to work yesterday.
options.explanation: Incorrect. This is past continuous, not present continuous.

options.text: Rishi will be driving to work tomorrow.
options.explanation: Incorrect. This is future continuous.

options.text: Rishi has driven to work today.
options.explanation: Incorrect. This is present perfect tense.

questions.correctAnswer: Rishi is driving to work today.
questions.explanation: Present continuous tense follows the structure subject + is/am/are + verb-ing ('is driving').

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the comparative degree of the adjective in bracket: The natural nightingale was considered ___ (treasured) than the jewelled bird by the Emperor in the end.
questions.hint: Use 'more' for multi-syllable adjectives in the comparative degree.
questions.correctAnswer: more treasured
questions.explanation: Multi-syllabic adjectives form their comparative degree by prefixing 'more'.

questions.question: Choose the superlative degree form of 'plain' to complete the sentence: Among all the colourful birds in China, the nightingale appeared the ___ in exterior plumage.
questions.hint: Add '-est' to form the superlative degree of a single-syllable adjective.

options.text: plainest
options.explanation: Correct. 'Plainest' is the regular superlative degree of the single-syllable adjective 'plain'.

options.text: most plain
options.explanation: Incorrect. Single-syllable adjectives take the '-est' suffix.

options.text: plainer
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'Plainer' is comparative, not superlative.

options.text: plainful
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'Plainful' is not a valid English word form.

questions.correctAnswer: plainest
questions.explanation: The superlative degree of 'plain' is 'plainest', used when comparing one against all members of a group.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct degree of the adjective: The mechanical nightingale had a ___ (predictable) rhythm than the woodland bird.
questions.hint: Comparative degree comparing two things using 'than'.
questions.correctAnswer: more predictable
questions.explanation: When comparing two entities using 'than', the comparative form of the polysyllabic adjective 'predictable' is 'more predictable'.

questions.question: Identify the proper sentence demonstrating the correct use of degrees of comparison:
questions.hint: Avoid double comparatives such as 'more prettier'.

options.text: The artificial bird was prettier than the real one.
options.explanation: Correct. 'Prettier' is the grammatically accurate comparative form of 'pretty'.

options.text: The artificial bird was more prettier than the real one.
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'More prettier' is an incorrect double comparative.

options.text: The artificial bird was prettiest than the real one.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Superlative 'prettiest' cannot be used with 'than' for two items.

options.text: The artificial bird was most pretty of the two.
options.explanation: Incorrect. When comparing two items, the comparative degree is required.

questions.correctAnswer: The artificial bird was prettier than the real one.
questions.explanation: 'Prettier' correctly modifies two items in comparison without using redundant modifiers like 'more'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with a suitable coordinating conjunction: The gentleman searched everywhere, ___ no one in the palace had heard of the bird.
questions.hint: Use a conjunction showing contrast.
questions.correctAnswer: but
questions.explanation: 'But' connects two contrasting independent clauses showing that despite searching everywhere, nobody knew the bird.

questions.question: Choose the correlative conjunction pair to complete the sentence: 'The courtiers admired ___ the mechanical design ___ the shiny exterior of the toy bird.'
questions.hint: Find the correlative pair that joins two parallel positive elements.

options.text: both ... and
options.explanation: Correct. 'Both ... and' properly pairs two complementary parallel nouns.

options.text: neither ... or
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'Neither' must pair with 'nor', not 'or'.

options.text: either ... and
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'Either' pairs with 'or'.

options.text: not only ... also
options.explanation: Incorrect. The required pair is 'not only ... but also'.

questions.correctAnswer: both ... and
questions.explanation: 'Both ... and' is a standard correlative conjunction coordinating two balanced noun phrases.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with an appropriate subordinating conjunction of time: The Emperor recovered his strength ___ the living nightingale began its song.
questions.hint: Use a conjunction indicating 'at the moment that' or 'after'.
questions.correctAnswer: as
questions.explanation: 'As' or 'when' functions as a subordinating conjunction of time linking the recovery to the singing.

questions.question: Select the sentence that uses a subordinating conjunction of concession correctly:
questions.hint: Look for words like 'although' or 'even though'.

options.text: Although the living nightingale was plain in appearance, its melodious song touched every heart.
options.explanation: Correct. 'Although' introduces a subordinate clause of concession.

options.text: The nightingale was plain however it sang with immense sweetness.
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'However' is a conjunctive adverb requiring a semicolon or new sentence.

options.text: Because the nightingale was plain, its song touched every heart.
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'Because' indicates cause, not concession.

options.text: The bird was plain so it sang melodiously.
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'So' expresses result, not concession.

questions.correctAnswer: Although the living nightingale was plain in appearance, its melodious song touched every heart.
questions.explanation: 'Although' introduces a concession clause demonstrating contrast between the bird's plain appearance and sublime song.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: The Emperor lay ___ his grand royal bed, deserted by the courtiers.
questions.hint: Identify the preposition of position for resting on a surface or in bed.
questions.correctAnswer: in
questions.explanation: We say 'in bed' to refer to a person lying tucked under covers or resting inside a bed.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition to complete the sentence: The father and son planted a ficus tree ___ the month of April.
questions.hint: Which preposition of time is used with months?

options.text: in
options.explanation: Correct. 'In' is used before months, seasons, and years.

options.text: on
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'On' is used for specific days and dates (e.g., on 19 September).

options.text: at
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'At' indicates specific clock times.

options.text: during to
options.explanation: Incorrect. This is an ungrammatical construction.

questions.correctAnswer: in
questions.explanation: Preposition 'in' is used when referring to months ('in the month of April').

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: The little kitchen maid rested ___ the woods while delivering food to her mother.
questions.hint: Preposition denoting location inside an area.
questions.correctAnswer: in
questions.explanation: 'In' is the proper preposition of place indicating location within an enclosed wooded area.

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates the correct use of prepositions of direction and location?
questions.hint: Check prepositions indicating movement towards and positioning beside.

options.text: The bird flew through the window and rested upon the bough of a tree beside the palace.
options.explanation: Correct. 'Through', 'upon', and 'beside' are used with grammatical precision.

options.text: The bird flew across of the window and perched above on the tree.
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'Across of' and 'above on' are improper compound prepositions.

options.text: The bird flew into the window and stayed between the sky.
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'Between' requires two distinct reference points.

options.text: The bird flew over into the room and settled onto the wall.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Awkward prepositional chaining.

questions.correctAnswer: The bird flew through the window and rested upon the bough of a tree beside the palace.
questions.explanation: 'Through' denotes motion into and out of an opening, 'upon' denotes surface resting, and 'beside' denotes next to.

questions.question: Correct the grammatical error in the given sentence.
questions.hint: Check the subject-verb agreement for the compound subject.
questions.inputSentence: The Emperor and his gentleman was searching for the hidden songbird.
questions.correctAnswer: The Emperor and his gentleman were searching for the hidden songbird.
questions.explanation: Two subjects connected by 'and' form a plural subject, requiring the plural auxiliary verb 'were'.

questions.question: Correct the tense consistency error in the given sentence.
questions.hint: Both verbs in past coordinate clauses must be in the past tense.
questions.inputSentence: When the watchmaker arrived, he examine the broken gears carefully.
questions.correctAnswer: When the watchmaker arrived, he examined the broken gears carefully.
questions.explanation: The main clause must match the past tense context established by 'arrived', changing 'examine' to 'examined'.

questions.question: Correct the pronoun and preposition error in the given sentence.
questions.hint: Identify the correct preposition for resting on a branch and objective pronoun case.
questions.inputSentence: The bird sat at the golden perch and sang for he.
questions.correctAnswer: The bird sat on the golden perch and sang for him.
questions.explanation: 'On' is used for a surface/perch, and the objective pronoun 'him' must follow the preposition 'for'.

questions.question: Change the following sentence from Active to Passive Voice.
questions.hint: Make 'a letter' the subject of the passive construction.
questions.inputSentence: The Emperor commanded a grand performance.
questions.correctAnswer: A grand performance was commanded by the Emperor.
questions.explanation: Simple past active 'commanded' becomes 'was commanded' in passive voice with the object becoming the subject.

questions.question: Change the following sentence from Passive to Active Voice.
questions.hint: Identify who performed the action ('the little maid') and place them as the subject.
questions.inputSentence: The courtiers were led to the woods by the little maid.
questions.correctAnswer: The little maid led the courtiers to the woods.
questions.explanation: The agent 'the little maid' becomes the subject, and 'were led' converts to the simple past active verb 'led'.

questions.question: Change the following sentence from Active to Passive Voice.
questions.hint: In continuous passive voice, use 'was/were being + past participle'.
questions.inputSentence: Bawihpuia's mother was watering the vegetable plants.
questions.correctAnswer: The vegetable plants were being watered by Bawihpuia's mother.
questions.explanation: Past continuous active 'was watering' becomes 'were being watered' when the plural object 'plants' becomes the subject.

questions.question: Rearrange the jumbled words into a meaningful, grammatically correct sentence.
questions.hint: Begin with the subject 'The music master' and find the main verb.
questions.correctAnswer: The music master praised the predictable mechanics of the artificial bird.
questions.explanation: Proper English syntax follows Subject ('The music master') + Verb ('praised') + Object phrase ('the predictable mechanics of the artificial bird').

questions.question: According to the passage, what material was the Emperor's palace made of?
questions.hint: Look at the first sentence of the passage describing the palace.

options.text: Delicate porcelain
options.explanation: Correct. The passage states the palace was made of delicate porcelain.

options.text: Polished marble
options.explanation: Incorrect. The text specifically names delicate porcelain.

options.text: Solid granite
options.explanation: Incorrect. Porcelain is mentioned, not granite.

options.text: Carved sandalwood
options.explanation: Incorrect. The text does not mention sandalwood for the palace.

questions.correctAnswer: Delicate porcelain
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states: 'the Emperor lived in the world's most beautiful palace, made of delicate porcelain.'

questions.question: Who paused his nocturnal work by the shore to admire the singing of the nightingale?
questions.hint: Check who was pulling in nets at night.

options.text: A poor fisherman
options.explanation: Correct. The text notes that even the poor fisherman pulling nets paused to listen.

options.text: The gentleman-in-waiting
options.explanation: Incorrect. The gentleman had never heard of the bird.

options.text: The chief gardener
options.explanation: Incorrect. The gardener is not mentioned in this extract.

options.text: A foreign merchant
options.explanation: Incorrect. Travellers admired it, but the person pulling nets was the fisherman.

questions.correctAnswer: A poor fisherman
questions.explanation: The text mentions: 'even the poor fisherman, busy pulling in his nets at night, would pause to listen.'

questions.question: Why did the Emperor summon his gentleman-in-waiting?
questions.hint: Consider the Emperor's reaction after reading books about his kingdom.

options.text: To demand why he had never been informed about the nightingale
options.explanation: Correct. The Emperor was astonished that he had to learn about his realm's greatest treasure from a book.

options.text: To order the renovation of the porcelain palace
options.explanation: Incorrect. The summons was specifically about the bird.

options.text: To punish travellers who visited his garden
options.explanation: Incorrect. Travellers praised the realm and were not being punished.

options.text: To purchase an artificial mechanical singing bird
options.explanation: Incorrect. The mechanical bird arrived later as a gift.

questions.correctAnswer: To demand why he had never been informed about the nightingale
questions.explanation: The Emperor exclaimed, 'There's said to be a marvellous bird called a nightingale here... Why wasn't I told?' and summoned his official.

questions.question: Describe the Emperor's garden as depicted in the passage, noting how far it extended.
questions.hint: Mention the flowers, silver bells, forest, and sea.
questions.correctAnswer: The Emperor's garden was wondrous and filled with extraordinary flowers, some of which had tiny silver bells that tinkled gently. It was so vast that it stretched into a great forest with tall trees and deep lakes, reaching down to the blue sea.
questions.explanation: The passage details the wondrous flowers with tinkling silver bells and explains that the garden extended into a dense forest with lakes that reached all the way to the blue sea.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the word **'porcelain'** as used in the passage?
questions.hint: Think of fine, delicate ceramic material.

options.text: A delicate, fine, translucent ceramic material
options.explanation: Correct. Porcelain refers to fine ceramic made by heating clay.

options.text: Rough uncut timber from the forest
options.explanation: Incorrect. Porcelain is a refined ceramic substance, not wood.

options.text: A thick sheet of heavy iron
options.explanation: Incorrect. Porcelain is brittle and refined, not metallic.

options.text: A coarse fabric used for royal robes
options.explanation: Incorrect. Porcelain is hard ceramic, not fabric.

questions.correctAnswer: A delicate, fine, translucent ceramic material
questions.explanation: Porcelain is a delicate, translucent vitrified ceramic material used for decorative and royal architecture.

questions.question: What is the contextual meaning of the word **'summoned'** in the passage?
questions.hint: The Emperor called upon an official with authority.

options.text: Authoritatively called or sent for someone to appear
options.explanation: Correct. To summon means to command an official or person to attend.

options.text: Exiled someone permanently from the city
options.explanation: Incorrect. That means banished, not summoned.

options.text: Forgave someone for failing their duties
options.explanation: Incorrect. Summoned does not indicate forgiveness.

options.text: Whispered secretly to an attendant
options.explanation: Incorrect. Summoning is a formal royal call.

questions.correctAnswer: Authoritatively called or sent for someone to appear
questions.explanation: 'Summoned' means urgently and officially ordered a person to come to one's presence.

questions.question: What does the word **'obsession'** mean as used in the extract from *Dad...*?
questions.hint: Consider the child's uncontrollable habit of scribbling on every surface.

options.text: An intense, persistent preoccupation or overwhelming desire
options.explanation: Correct. The passage defines obsession as an intense, persistent urge to do something.

options.text: A mild disinterest in creative activities
options.explanation: Incorrect. Obsession indicates excessive focus, not disinterest.

options.text: A sudden feeling of sorrow or grief
options.explanation: Incorrect. It relates to passion and persistent habit, not sorrow.

options.text: The act of obeying parental instructions promptly
options.explanation: Incorrect. Bawihpuia was scribbling despite rules.

questions.correctAnswer: An intense, persistent preoccupation or overwhelming desire
questions.explanation: In the text, 'obsession' denotes Bawihpuia's overwhelming compulsion to write and scribble on every surface.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the appropriate vocabulary word from *The Nightingale*: When the morning mist cleared, the spectre ___ into thin air, leaving peace behind.
questions.hint: Choose a word meaning 'disappeared completely' (vanished / restored).
questions.correctAnswer: vanished
questions.explanation: 'Vanished' means disappeared suddenly and completely, as Death vanished like mist.

questions.question: What does the idiomatic phrase **'brings tears to my eyes'** express when the kitchen maid speaks of the nightingale's music?
questions.hint: Does it mean physical eye irritation or deep emotional moving?

options.text: Evokes deep emotional feeling and poignant joy
options.explanation: Correct. The phrase signifies being deeply touched and moved emotionally.

options.text: Causes intense ocular pain and discomfort
options.explanation: Incorrect. It is a metaphorical expression of poignant emotion, not physical pain.

options.text: Indicates extreme physical weariness from work
options.explanation: Incorrect. The tears are caused by the beauty of the song.

options.text: Shows anger and disappointment at royal commands
options.explanation: Incorrect. It signifies positive aesthetic wonder.

questions.correctAnswer: Evokes deep emotional feeling and poignant joy
questions.explanation: 'Brings tears to one's eyes' is an idiom expressing profound emotional resonance and tenderness.

questions.question: What did the Emperor mean when he called the nightingale's music his **'greatest treasure'**?
questions.hint: Contrast material wealth with priceless natural art.

options.text: The most precious and invaluable wonder of his entire empire
options.explanation: Correct. It means the song was more priceless than gold, jewels, or palaces.

options.text: A chest containing gold coins buried in the forest
options.explanation: Incorrect. The treasure was the living bird and its song.

options.text: A secret book sent by foreign monarchs
options.explanation: Incorrect. The book described the treasure, but wasn't the treasure itself.

options.text: A jewel-studded mechanical toy kept in the vault
options.explanation: Incorrect. The mechanical bird was sent much later.

questions.correctAnswer: The most precious and invaluable wonder of his entire empire
questions.explanation: 'Greatest treasure' metaphorically designates the song of the nightingale as superior to all material possessions.

questions.question: Match the difficult words and phrases from Column A with their correct contextual meanings in Column B.
questions.hint: Check the story vocabulary notes for perch, footmen, and siesta.
columnB: (a) Servants who accompany and attend to someone
(b) A short afternoon nap or rest
(c) A small stand or rod where a bird can rest or sit
questions.explanation: A 'Perch' is a rod where a bird rests (c); 'Footmen' are attendant servants (a); 'Siesta' is an afternoon nap (b).

questions.question: Match the words and regional expressions from Column A with their accurate contextual definitions in Column B.
questions.hint: Look at the glossaries from both chapters including northeastern cultural words.
columnB: (a) Scolded or rebuked for a wrongdoing
(b) Sent away or expelled from a realm as punishment
(c) The lower part of the house or yard in the Northeast
questions.explanation: 'Banished' means expelled/sent away (b); 'Kawmthlang' refers to the lower part of the house in Mizo culture (c); 'Reprimanded' means scolded (a).

questions.question: In the story *Dad...*, with what instrument did Bawihpuia attempt to write his name on the refrigerator?
questions.hint: His mother was stitching nearby when he picked it up.

options.text: A fallen sewing needle
options.explanation: Correct. Bawihpuia picked up a fallen needle from the floor while his mother was stitching.

options.text: A blue ballpoint pen
options.explanation: Incorrect. No pen was available to him.

options.text: A piece of coloured chalk
options.explanation: Incorrect. He used a needle found in the kitchen.

options.text: A sharp pencil
options.explanation: Incorrect. He picked up a fallen needle.

questions.correctAnswer: A fallen sewing needle
questions.explanation: The text mentions: 'He picked up a fallen needle and started to write, "My name is ..." on the fridge when I spotted him.'

questions.question: What crucial principle did the father teach his son during the bedroom counsel?
questions.hint: Focus on the explanation given about the purpose of objects.

options.text: Every tool has its specific purpose and should not be misused.
options.explanation: Correct. The father explained that needles are meant for stitching, and tools have designated functions.

options.text: Children should never engage in drawing or writing.
options.explanation: Incorrect. He reprimanded the misuse of the needle on paint, not artistic passion.

options.text: The refrigerator was too inexpensive to care for.
options.explanation: Incorrect. He explained it would be costly to repaint.

options.text: Drawing with chalk is preferred over pencils.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Chalk was not part of the discussion.

questions.correctAnswer: Every tool has its specific purpose and should not be misused.
questions.explanation: The father explicitly counseled: 'every tool had its specific purpose, and that he should not repeat what he had done.'

questions.question: How did Bawihpuia react to his father's reprimand, and what noticeable change occurred in his habits afterward?
questions.hint: Mention his eye contact and how wall scribblings changed.
questions.correctAnswer: Bawihpuia looked straight at his father while being counseled. Afterward, the father noticed that the scribblings and writings on the walls and other surfaces gradually started to decrease.
questions.explanation: The text states that Bawihpuia listened attentively, looking straight at his father, and subsequently, his habit of writing on walls and household surfaces decreased.

questions.question: Why did the courtiers initially mistake a mooing cow and croaking frogs for the nightingale?
questions.hint: Think about whether the courtiers had ever stepped outside the palace into nature.

options.text: They had lived sheltered lives in the palace and had never heard a nightingale before.
options.explanation: Correct. Having never visited the forest or heard nature, they were completely ignorant of the bird's true call.

options.text: The nightingale was intentionally mimicking other animals to deceive them.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The nightingale does not mimic frogs or cattle.

options.text: The kitchen maid deliberately pointed them to the wrong animals.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The kitchen maid had to correct their foolish mistakes.

options.text: The Emperor had instructed them to bring back any noisy creature.
options.explanation: Incorrect. They were specifically searching for the nightingale.

questions.correctAnswer: They had lived sheltered lives in the palace and had never heard a nightingale before.
questions.explanation: The courtiers were so detached from nature and had never heard the bird that they mistook common farm and pond sounds for the nightingale.

questions.question: What caused the jewelled artificial nightingale to stop singing permanently?
questions.hint: Recall what happened inside its mechanical body after a year of continuous use.

options.text: Its internal gears broke with a 'whizz' and 'whirr' due to being worn out.
options.explanation: Correct. Something broke inside with a whizz and whirr, leaving it worn out and silent.

options.text: The Emperor threw it out of the window in disgust.
options.explanation: Incorrect. It was kept on a cushion beside his bed.

options.text: The watchmaker accidentally lost its key.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The watchmaker mended it partially, but its gears were worn out.

options.text: The courtiers stole its diamonds and rubies.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The jewels remained intact; the internal mechanism broke.

questions.correctAnswer: Its internal gears broke with a 'whizz' and 'whirr' due to being worn out.
questions.explanation: After a year of repetitive playing, something snapped inside the mechanical bird with a whizz and whirr, wearing out the inner clockwork.

questions.question: How did the living nightingale persuade Death to return the Emperor's royal insignia (crown, sword, and banner)?
questions.hint: What exchange took place between the bird and Death?

options.text: It sang exquisitely of nature and quiet graveyards, demanding an item back for each song.
options.explanation: Correct. Death surrendered the sword, banner, and crown one by one in exchange for each beautiful song.

options.text: It threatened Death with the Emperor's imperial army.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The bird used its art and melody, not force.

options.text: It offered the jewelled mechanical bird to Death in exchange.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Death ignored the broken artificial bird.

options.text: It brought healing medicinal herbs from the great forest.
options.explanation: Incorrect. It cured the Emperor solely through the emotional and spiritual power of its music.

questions.correctAnswer: It sang exquisitely of nature and quiet graveyards, demanding an item back for each song.
questions.explanation: Death listened captivated to the nightingale's songs of peace and graveyards, relinquishing the Emperor's sword, banner, and crown one by one.

questions.question: What condition did the nightingale lay down before promising to visit and sing for the Emperor regularly?
questions.hint: What secret did the bird ask the Emperor to keep from his court?
questions.correctAnswer: The nightingale asked the Emperor to keep one promise: to tell no one that he had a little bird who visited him and told him everything about what was happening across his empire.
questions.explanation: The bird insisted on freedom and confidentiality: 'promise one thing: tell no one you have a little bird who tells you everything. It is better so.'

questions.question: In Zirsangkima's story *Dad...*, why did the narrator find his six-year-old son's questions both challenging and deeply meaningful?
questions.hint: Mention Bawihpuia's innocent inquiries about God, love, and discipline.
questions.correctAnswer: The narrator found the questions challenging because they tackled deep existential and moral concepts—such as why God doesn't have a phone or whether a teacher scolding a student means lack of love. They showed the child's sincere effort to comprehend human relationships and find beauty in life.
questions.explanation: Bawihpuia's questions were simple yet profound, challenging adult assumptions and proving that the young boy was striving to understand love, compassion, and divine connection.

questions.question: Contrast the music master's evaluation of the artificial bird with the living nightingale. What does this reveal about his character?
questions.hint: Focus on predictable mechanics versus emotional spontaneity.
questions.correctAnswer: The music master praised the artificial bird because its mechanics were predictable, calculable, and perfectly ordered, unlike the mysterious, spontaneous singing of the living bird. This highlights that he prioritized superficial perfection and rigid order over authentic feeling and soul.
questions.explanation: The music master valued technical exactness and predictability over authentic expression, illustrating the limitation of valuing artificial conformity over natural art.

questions.question: How does the story *The Nightingale* highlight the central theme that genuine affection and art cannot be bought or held captive?
questions.hint: Discuss the golden perch/cage versus the bird returning freely to save the Emperor from Death.
questions.correctAnswer: The story demonstrates this theme through the nightingale's refusal of golden slippers and rejection of the cage and footmen. True art thrives only in freedom. When the Emperor tried to confine the bird, it flew away; yet when he was dying, it returned out of voluntary compassion. The bird prized tears of sincere emotion over royal crowns and precious gems.
questions.explanation: The nightingale's music lost its authentic power when confined. Its willing return on the deathbed showed that true devotion and art arise freely from love and empathy, not wealth or coercion.

questions.question: Explain the significance of the memory that echoes in the father's mind 'a decade later' in the story *Dad...*.
questions.hint: Connect the memory of the fridge scratch, the needle, and the boy's voice asking about the paint cost.
questions.correctAnswer: Ten years later, the father hears his own words about loving fellow human beings and respecting objects, immediately followed by the echo of his son's innocent voice asking, 'Dad, how much does the paint cost?'. This evokes both smiles and tears, highlighting parental nostalgia, the enduring bond between father and son, and the emotional pain of distance now that the boy lives in a faraway land.
questions.explanation: The memory symbolizes the bittersweet passage of time. The simple lesson taught in childhood remains etched in the father's heart, connecting him across miles to his grown son who has ventured far from home.

questions.question: Analyze how Andersen contrasts artificial beauty with natural simplicity in *The Nightingale*.
questions.hint: Contrast the glittering jewelled bird that broke down with the plain grey bird that conquered Death.
questions.correctAnswer: Andersen sharply contrasts the two birds: the artificial nightingale was glittery, studded with diamonds and sapphires, but could only repeat one rigid waltz until its fragile gears broke down. In contrast, the real nightingale was plain and grey, yet its spontaneous, soulful melody moved listeners to tears, healed the dying Emperor, and even banished Death itself.
questions.explanation: The contrast proves that superficial splendour and mass-produced mechanical art are transient and hollow, whereas natural, heartfelt simplicity holds lasting power, vitality, and emotional depth.
